article.Citation/Title: O'Reilly, P. O., & Funk, A. (1964). LSD in chronic alcoholism. Canadian Psychiatric Association Journal, 9(3), 258-261.
article.Outcome: 38% abstinence (26/68) at follow-up; single-arm, no comparator
article.InterventionDescription: LSD 200 gamma (mcg), single oral dose, ward-based on day 6-7 of admission; 5-6 hour supervised session with nurse/therapist; embedded in milieu therapy.

ae_events.Description: Physical distress (unspecified physical symptoms) noted in some patients around the LSD session, per clinical records used for follow-up correlates
Post-treatment disturbance (confusion and/or depression) noted in some patients following the LSD session, per clinical records
Paranoid psychotic reaction requiring hospitalization in one of 68 patients; authors found no evidence linking it to the LSD experience

article.Outcome: Findings section: 'Twenty-six patients, or 38% of the total group were found to be abstaining from alcohol in the two months preceding follow-up' (26/68). This is the article's sole quantitative treatment-outcome result (no comparator group exists), consistent with the Summary. The secondary correlate finding (46% of abstainers vs 6% of non-abstainers showed the depression/transcendental-experience pattern) is a predictor analysis, not the primary treatment outcome, so it was not chosen as Outcome.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic is reported alongside the 38% abstinence proportion itself; the only significance testing reported ('.01 level of significance') attaches to the depression/transcendental-experience correlate analysis, a different (secondary) analysis, so it cannot be paired with Outcome. Coded '.'.
article.PVal: No p-value is reported for the primary abstinence proportion (26/68 = 38%) itself; the article states only that 'there was no significant change in abstinence... between the two periods' (a different, within-subject comparison), without a printed p-value or threshold. Coded '.'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 68 is the denominator the authors themselves used for the headline rate: 26/68 = 38% ('Twenty-six patients, or 38% of the total group'). This is despite the separate note that 'complete information was available on all but seven patients' (61/68) — that 61/68 figure describes data-completeness, not the denominator used for Outcome.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Objective, design (three-source follow-up methodology), setting (Union Hospital, Moose Jaw), eligibility (no psychosis, voluntary), intervention (200 gamma LSD protocol), outcomes, statistical methods (.01 threshold stated), results, and harms are all described. Comparator, sample-size/power, randomization, and blinding are never discussed even as absent (single-arm design is never explicitly framed as a limitation), and no funding/COI statement appears anywhere. 9 of 14 met, below the 13-of-14 threshold for binary=1.

article.EligibleYN: Coded Y under the single-arm/open-label boundary case: the Introduction frames the program as 'a study of the effectiveness of this treatment' with a standardized, previously-published protocol, defined enrollment criteria (no psychosis, voluntary acceptance), an assigned regimen (200 gamma LSD, day 6-7), and a structured, pre-specified follow-up methodology (three independent information sources, three defined sampling windows) — satisfying criterion (a) despite the follow-up itself being executed via retrospective/cross-sectional questionnaire rather than fixed-interval prospective visits. Criterion (b) is clearly met (abstinence rate as the reported outcome).
article.Pos Result Y/N: No comparator exists, so judged on the study's own pre/post framing: the Discussion states the treatment 'produced sobriety in 38% of patients without any disastrous side effects,' which the authors themselves present as a positive result. Coded 1.
article.PrimaryCare: 26 of 68 referrals came from the Bureau of Alcoholism and 42 from private physicians, but this describes only the referral source, not an interface between the treatment/study itself and primary-care settings or providers — treatment was entirely psychiatric-ward-based. Coded 0.
article.Retention (%): Study was not randomized, so denominator is the enrolled N=68. 'Complete information was available on all but seven patients' → 61/68 = 89.7%, used as Retention (%). This reflects follow-up data completeness rather than treatment dropout, since nearly all patients completed the single LSD session before discharge.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: No validated psychometric scale or SUD instrument (e.g., AUDIT, ASI) is named anywhere; abstinence status was determined via questionnaire and corroborating-source report, not a standardized instrument. Coded 0.
article.ConfoundYN: Findings section statistically tested age, marital status, educational level, AA/church membership, years of uncontrolled drinking, psychiatric diagnosis, number of prior psychiatric treatments, and treating psychiatrist as potential correlates of abstinence (all non-significant except the depression/transcendental-experience factor). Coded 1.
article.BaseStatus: 62% of the cohort was diagnosed 'Chronic Alcoholism,' ~60% had been drinking uncontrolledly >10 years, and all were admitted to an inpatient psychiatric ward for treatment, indicating a severe, treatment-resistant baseline population. Coded 'Severe'.
article.Age_Median: Mean age 37 (range 20-62) falls in the 30-50 bracket.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Race/ethnicity of the sample is not reported anywhere in the article. Coded '.'.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Study conducted at Union Hospital, Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, Canada. Coded 'NonUS'.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Sample was drawn from routine referrals (Bureau of Alcoholism and private physicians) to a hospital psychiatric ward — a real-world clinical alcoholism population — with the only exclusion being active psychosis, not a specially recruited or highly screened research-volunteer sample. Coded 1.
article.Followup in months: Article reports 'a range of two to 34 months had elapsed since treatment, with a mean of 14 months' at the time of the cross-sectional follow-up survey; 34 months (the maximum) is used as the longest reported follow-up duration. Note this is the maximum elapsed time across a cross-sectional cohort survey, not a fixed protocol endpoint.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Presence/absence of 'depression' and 'transcendental experience' was recorded from psychiatric/nursing notes and used as a correlate of abstinence, so a mental-health-related dimension was assessed, though not via a validated scale (see ValidatedScaleMeasYN=0). Coded 1.
article.Implementation Outcome: Article reports that 'only two patients... indicated that, given free choice, they would not receive LSD again' — an acceptability outcome. Coded 1.
article.ReductionMeasured: Article explicitly states non-abstainers were classed as such 'whether or not they showed some improvement,' i.e., partial reduction was not separately quantified or reported as a distinct outcome. Coded 0.
article.RelapseMeasured: Abstinence was compared between the 2-month post-treatment window and the last 2 months of the follow-up period specifically to detect change/relapse over time ('no significant change in abstinence or indulgence between the two periods'), and patients with repeat LSD treatments were analyzed on their most recent episode. Coded 1.
article.SafetyReported / HarmsAssessed: The article devotes discussion to adverse effects (citing Cohen & Ditman 1963) and reports its own safety findings (1/68 hospitalized for a psychotic reaction, plus physical-distress/post-treatment-disturbance correlates), so harms were assessed. SafetyReported='Y' and HarmsAssessed=1 per the required agreement rule.
article.NParticipantsWithAE / AE_denominator: AE_denominator=68, the full treated cohort ('out of 68 patients only one patient...'). NParticipantsWithAE is coded '.' because only the psychotic-reaction count (n=1) is explicit; the physical-distress and post-treatment-disturbance categories carry no reported counts, so a reliable aggregate participant count cannot be given.

ae_events.O'Reilly 1964_AE01: Findings section states the abstinence-correlated (better-outcome) group showed 'no signs of physical distress' at follow-up, implying some patients did display physical distress after LSD, but no count, description, or duration is given anywhere in the article. Graded Mild per the rubric's default for under-specified AEs; SeverityIndeterminate=Y because no intervention/impairment/duration detail exists to grade further. SeveritySource='rubric' since the authors (pre-1980, pre-CTCAE) never assigned this event a severity label themselves.
ae_events.O'Reilly 1964_AE02: Same Findings passage references 'post-treatment disturbance' as a negative correlate of abstinence, and the Discussion separately mentions 'confusion or depression' as possible post-treatment reactions; treated as one AE type (post-treatment psychological disturbance) since the article gives no distinct counts or descriptions separating confusion from depression. No count or duration given, so graded Mild by rubric default with SeverityIndeterminate=Y. AE_type='both' because depression/confusion in this context plausibly reflects unresolved challenging-experience integration (Discussion's own framing) as well as a clinical adverse reaction.
ae_events.O'Reilly 1964_AE03: Findings/Discussion state 1 of 68 patients developed a paranoid psychotic reaction requiring hospitalization; the authors explicitly note no evidence linking it to the LSD experience, but it occurred within the treated cohort and is reported in the article's own safety discussion, so it is retained here per the instruction not to understate harm. Hospitalization meets an FDA seriousness criterion, so it is graded Severe with confidence (SeverityIndeterminate=N). Onset timing relative to treatment is not stated (discovered via the follow-up survey, elapsed time up to 34 months), so Onset='unknown'. SeveritySource='rubric' because the authors reported only the fact of hospitalization, not a severity/SAE label, and this is a pre-1980 article predating CTCAE.

config_proposal.note: Single-arm, no-comparator follow-up survey; the reported 38% (26/68) abstinence proportion has no counterpart group, so none of the seven supported conversion methods (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, RR) apply. No comparator exists to compute an odds ratio from two-group proportions.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: 38% abstinence (26/68) at follow-up (mean 14 months post-treatment), explicitly framed by the authors as having 'produced sobriety... without any disastrous side effects' — a positive pre/post result in a single-arm design.
